newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to sell "Big Three" banks by June 97 - paper.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to sell "Big Three" banks by June 97 - paper.

text.p: Taiwan's finance ministry has decided to sell some of its holdings in the "Big Three" commercial banks by the end of June 1997 to alleviate the government's budget deficit, newspapers said on Sunday.

The ministry's selldown plan on Chang Hwa, First Commercial and Hua Nan, would bring an estimated T$3.7 billion to state coffers, the Commercial Times newspaper quoted finance ministry officials as saying.

Previously, the ministry had planned to sell T$1.837 billion worth of First Commercial shares at the price of T$176 per share, T$233 million worth of Hua Nan at T$188 each and T$1.632 billion worth of Chang Hwa at T$184 a share.

The newspaper did not say what the new selling price targets for the three banks might be, but officials were quoted as saying the ministry would try to minimise the impact of the sale to the stock market.
On Saturday, Chang Hwa, First Commercial, and Hua Nan closed at T$157, T$167, and T$127.50, respectively.
The government, dogged by a shortfall in tax revenue in a slowing economy in the first three quarters, has forecast a 1996 deficit of T$87.6 billion.
